content: Born into the Śākya clan through skillful means and compassion,Invincible, you who conquered the hosts of Māra,With a body as majestic as a mountain of gold—To that King of the Śākyas, I prostrate.Having first aroused the mind for enlightenment,You perfected the two accumulations of merit and wisdom;Now, through your vast deeds for the sake of beings,I offer praise to you, who have become their protector.Having perceived the time to tame those to be tamed among the gods,You descended from the divine realm and approached like a great elephant;Having observed the noble lineage, you entered the womb of the goddess Māyādevī—To you, I prostrate.When the ten months were complete, the Prince of the ŚākyasWas born in the auspicious Lumbinī Grove;To you, whose supreme marks were honored by Brahmā and Indra,And who confirmed your destiny for enlightenment, I prostrate.That youthful, powerful lion among men,Demonstrated his mastery of the arts in Aṅga and Magadha;Having humbled all those who were full of pride,To you, who became without rival, I prostrate.To act in accordance with worldly custom,And to avoid any reproach, you took a retinue of consorts;To you who, through such skillful means,Governed the kingdom, I prostrate.Seeing that the activities of cyclic existence are without essence,You departed from the household and traveled through the sky;To you who ordained yourself before the Viśuddha Stūpa,And took up the life of renunciation, I prostrate.Intending to achieve enlightenment through diligence,On the banks of the Nairañjanā for six years,You practiced austerities and perfected perseverance;To you who attained supreme meditative concentration, I prostrate.To make meaningful the efforts made since beginningless time,Beneath the Bodhi tree in Magadha,You sat in an unmoving cross-legged posture and became a manifest Buddha;To you who perfected enlightenment, I prostrate.Having swiftly gazed upon beings with compassion,In supreme places such as Vārāṇasī,You turned the wheel of Dharma and, for those to be trained,Established them in the three vehicles; to you I prostrate.Having suppressed the malicious attacks of others,The six non-Buddhist teachers, Devadatta, and the rest,And having vanquished the maras in the land of Vārāṇasī,To you, the Sage victorious in battle, I prostrate.With qualities unparalleled throughout the three realms,You displayed great miracles at Śrāvastī;Highly venerated by all beings, gods and humans alike,To you who caused the teachings to flourish, I prostrate.In order to urge the indolent toward the Dharma,Upon the pure ground of the town of Kuśinagara,You dissolved your immortal, vajra-like body;To you who passed into nirvāṇa, I prostrate.Although you perceived that in reality there is no perishing,In order that future sentient beings might accumulate merit,You emanated a multitude of relics in that very place;To you who divided your remains into eight portions, I prostrate.Through the virtue of this brief praise,Of the deeds of the Bhagavan, Master of the Teachings,May the conduct of all wandering beingsBecome equal to the deeds of the Sugata himself.O Tathāgata, whatever your physical form may be,Your retinue, the span of your life, and your pure realm,And whatever your supreme and excellent marks may be,May I and all others become exactly like that.By the power of praising and supplicating you,In whatever region I and others may dwell,May sickness, harmful spirits, poverty, and strife be pacified,And please grant that the Dharma and auspiciousness increase.Through the Teacher appearing in the world,Through the teachings shining brightly like the sun,And through the great harmony of the followers who uphold the teachings,May there be the auspiciousness of the Dharma enduring for a long time.It is renowned that this was composed by the Drigung Kyobpa Jikten Sumgön.
